title: Riska Boy
text: “Curious about why I’m here, despyon?”
“Yes, that’s exactly what I’ve been asking this whole time!”
“That would be… despyon…”
I held up a single finger to my lips as if to say “it’s a secret,” then paralyzed Itsuki with a Paralyze Lance VII faster than the eye could follow.
“Guah!? Wh— what are—”
Having him shout would be a hassle. Of course, I’d been fully prepared to paralyze him the instant he tried to raise his voice. Itsuki went stiff and slumped right down where he stood.
“I figured I’d teach the truth of this country to you, getting all cocky while dancing to the kingdom’s tune, despyoooon.”
“By the command of the usaunny, source of power! Decipher creation anew, and alter the form of this one!”
“Faerie Morph! Despyoon!”
And with that, I hit Itsuki with Faerie Morph, the spell that turns its target into a pioneer fairy. I was curious what it would do to someone at his particular stage, honestly.
“Itsuki-kun’s an idiot, so it’s time for a little study session, despyoon!”
“Wh— aaaaah…!?”

With a poof, Itsuki transformed into a shape I recognized well: a riska. His clothes fell right off. There, now you’re Riska Itsuki. Get in water and your cheek pouches puff up, and you fly through the sky with a flamethrower. If being human meant he couldn’t understand just how hard Father’s circumstances had been, then surely spending some time in a non-human form would make it clear. That way, I figured, he’d be able to see through the Crimson Swine’s lies at a glance.
“Wh-what… is… this!?”

Itsuki seemed shocked at his own transformed body. He probably felt like everything had changed, but really it was only his height and shape that were different, surprisingly enough. Well, the various special abilities would probably require clearing pioneer-zone dungeons to unlock. It was rather amusing how much more this form could do, actually. You could even double-jump, I say.
“You’ve become a riska, despyoon. Take a look at this country in that form, and I think you’ll understand what’s true, despyon.”
I strolled leisurely past Itsuki, numb and unable to move.
“W-wait… ugh…”
The paralyzed Riska Itsuki grabbed at the hem of my clothes, but I swatted his hand away and walked off without looking back.
“Well then, farewell, despyon. Pyoon pyon pyon pyoooon!”

Laughing a hearty “HAHAHA!” I slowly took my leave from the scene. Itsuki, still paralyzed, lay flat on his back right where he’d fallen. I gently closed the door behind me. Now, until the paralysis wore off, Itsuki wouldn’t be able to move, so nobody would find him. Incidentally, the moment I left the room, I went stealth with Cloaking Lance and slipped straight out of the inn. That cleared up some of my frustration, I must say. Surely something would be done about Itsuki’s clouded eyes now. It would be quite the spectacle to see whether he figured out what was true.
Now then, what else…
“Wide open, despyon!”
Hidden in the bushes, I ambushed Ren from behind.
“Hm? Guah!?”

Ren, ever the aloof one, had slipped out to go hunting while Kuro-chan was asleep, so I knocked him out cold with a surprise Sleep Lance X. Naturally, pinpointing his location was thanks to Kuro-chan, who’d been tailing him. All hail the monster crest, indeed. Sorry, Kuro-chan, but it would be a hassle if Ren kept moving around as usual.
“…Zzz…”
Fast asleep. He was so wide open he never even saw me coming. Well then, take this.
“Faerie Morph, despy— no wait, indeed.”

Still asleep, Ren transformed into an inult. It would look suspicious if only Itsuki had been turned into a pioneer fairy, after all, so I turned Ren into an inult too, for good measure. You know how it goes—Heroes turning one after another into mysterious creatures? Next target’s me or Father!? That kind of story, I imagine.

Now then. Let’s delay the discovery of this crime a little longer. After all, Ren always ends up heading to Zeltoble afterward anyway—that’s just his usual pattern. I grabbed the still-unconscious, inult-shaped Ren and headed to the harbor.

Then I stuffed him into a crate of cargo bound for Zeltoble, right alongside the kitchen knives that Father and Panda’s foster father use. It would be a hassle if Assistant’s or Rival’s parent got taken out, after all. If a second Rival ended up appearing as a result, it wouldn’t be funny in the slightest. No, having Rivals multiply across loop boundaries is simply out of the question. One more on top of the ones I already have—please, no. And besides, the original Rival was even more single-minded and creepy. The current Rival is a cunning schemer and troublesome in her own way, but… still, is the original Rival easier to deal with, I wonder? With a rattling clatter, the anchor was hoisted, and the ship bound for Zeltoble set sail.
“You go on and dominate the underground culinary world with Father’s group’s kitchen knives, indeed. FUHAHAHAHA!”
And so, having thoroughly dealt with both Ren and Itsuki, I slept soundly that night, resting easy. Zzz… indeed. A job well done, I say.
Oh? This place is…
“Man… just because you recognized it doesn’t mean you have to sink all the way down here just from sleeping. How deep are you gonna dive, honestly.”
When I came to, I found myself in Spirit of the Spear’s world, and Spirit of the Spear appeared before me looking utterly exasperated, calling out.
“What in the world is going on? Are we looping already?”
“We’re still mid-loop. You just fell down here because you’re sleeping so deeply. Honestly, playing such awful pranks on those two—how good did that feel, I wonder.”
“Honestly,” Spirit of the Spear muttered on, grumbling about something or other. Not my problem, I say.
“So I’ll return once I wake up, then?”
“Pretty much. Though, I tell you to do something you’ve never done before, and you sure run wild with it.”
“How’s that, I wonder?”
“…Suit yourself.”

Hmm… doesn’t seem the least bit fazed by that jab either, indeed. Guess I’ll just have to skewer every last one of those guys’ backsides with my spear, one after another, I mused, while wanting to get out of there as soon as possible—when I noticed, off in the distance, some sort of lively gathering of lights.
“What’s that, I wonder?”
“Ah, that’s a celebration for a spirit born of this world who’s become a high-tier spirit powerful enough to dwell within a Sacred Weapon like me.”
Ohh… so there are events like that, are there.
“This is your world, so that means it’s a subordinate spirit under you?”
“You actually fell into a slightly different place, so I just joined up with you right away. I just happened to be attending the celebration myself.”
Ohh… I see. So spirits hold celebrations too, apparently. As I thought that, two lights belonging to the spirits who were the guests of honor at the celebration noticed me and drew closer.
“Spirit of the Spear-sama, thank you so much for coming to our celebration today.”
“Yeah. Honestly, reaching this realm is genuinely praiseworthy on my part too. A time will come when you’ll set off on your own journey, but I believe you’ll manage it just fine.”
“Yes… please look after me, I humbly ask.”
So, Spirit of the Spear seemed to be speaking to one of the two spirits.
“And you’re going off for a while to train as Spirit of the Hammer, a god-slaying weapon, right? That other spirit’s coming over here to rest up, more or less.”
“Yes. I’m looking forward to reuniting with some familiar faces from the past. Well… though I suppose we’ll be able to talk, at least.”
The spirit destined to become Spirit of the Hammer… judging by the voice, sounded male. Why was that, I wondered? That voice sounded familiar somehow.
“Um, excuse me… could the one standing beside you perhaps be the Spear Hero-sama?”
So, the spirit who seemed to be the guest of honor noticed me and asked Spirit of the Spear as much. What was this, I wondered? This spirit too… felt somehow familiar to me as well.
